chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Bahr, from Mihzam Al-Asady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you take the oil upon your palm, say: 'O Allah, I ask You for beauty and adornment and love, and I seek refuge in You from disgrace, ugliness, and detestation.' Then place it on your forehead, beginning with what Allah began with.

key_terms.الدُّهْنَ: Oil or unguent used for anointing

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and method for applying oil according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith outlines the spiritual etiquette of grooming, linking physical adornment with inner divine favor through a specific supplication for beauty and love while seeking protection from disgrace. The instruction to begin on the forehead (ya'fukh) reflects the Shia emphasis on aligning bodily actions with cosmic order, as the forehead is the first part of the body to touch the ground in prostration (sujood). This practice underscores the integration of mundane acts with worship, transforming personal care into an act of remembrance.
